newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-LOMU OUT OF RUGBY FOR 6 MONTHS OR MORE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LOMU OUT OF RUGBY FOR 6 MONTHS OR MORE.

text.p: Rugby superstar Jonah Lomu said on Friday he had pulled out of rugby for at least six months to undergo treatment for a kidney ailment.
The condition, nephrotic syndrome, was first diagnosed two years ago as a mild abnormality, but monitoring has shown a moderate deterioration over the past three months.
"I feel very positive about the treatment," Lomu said at a news conference in Auckland called by the New Zealand Rugby Football Union (NZRFU).
"I've got the best doctors on the case and I never lie down and let anything trample over me. This is just a hiccup."
The kidney treatment means the giant winger would fail random drug tests.
Kidney specialists told Lomu treatment was essential. Lomu would begin the treatment, including intensive drug therapy, shortly and continue for six months.
Doctors have given him a 50 percent chance of full recovery.

All Black coach John Hart, who was at the news conference along with All Black doctor John Mayhew, Lomu's wife Tanya and his manager Phil Kingsley-Jones, said he expected Lomu back playing later this year.
"The hearts of the All Black management go out to Jonah -- he's had a tough year and we're hoping he'll be back in action for us soon," Hart said.
"It's a huge loss to the All Blacks. He's a huge star on the field and off the field and it's going to have a big impact," Hart said.

Lomu, who has been fighting to regain the form which took him to fame in the 1995 World Cup, had hoped to use the New Zealand Barbarians game against England in November as a springboard to relaunch his international rugby career.
He struggled with his form and injury on last year's tour of South Africa and lost his place in the test team.
Lomu said he had a history of slowly recovering from sickness and injury. As a boy he had taken a long time to overcome normal childhood sicknesses.
"I was just sick and tired of taking antibiotics," he said.
Officials said the illness should not affect Lomu's sponsorship contracts with a sportshoe company or the NZRFU.
